title: New Household Rules (Pt3?) #scary #fyp #trending #horrorstories #viral #animatic
analysis_notes: Downloaded on the Spark at 480x854 (format 135 + original en-US opus track 251-7; 2.9 MB, kept) to ~/studio/refs/horror/BciSW_2VMZg.mp4 with info.json, thumbnail and en auto-subs. Fresh metadata at 09:15 UTC: 103,714 views, 3,177 likes (3.1% like rate), 67 comments, no description, no tags. Transcript = YouTube auto-subs (word-timed, 135 words), matching the burned-in captions word for word; full timestamped transcript at research/library/transcripts/BciSW_2VMZg.txt. YouTube offers auto-dubbed audio in 7 languages (extra reach). Frames sampled at 2 fps; contact sheet at 1 fps. Format = 'rules horror' (second-person survival instructions, like the 'If you are alone at home, follow these rules' genre) in an 'animatic': mostly still AI-style anime/painterly illustrations, 16:9 inside a 9:16 black frame (letterbox), slow push-ins, crossfades, RGB-split glitch transitions and frequent hold-on-black text cards. Narration is a single calm voice (not checked by ear; auto-subs are clean, so it is likely clear TTS or a studio read). Audio mean -21 dB, peak 0 dB, only one gap >0.4 s (38.8-39.3 s, the dramatic pause before the reveal). 'Pt3?' implies a series; the box 'you're not ready for' is left open as a series hook. Do not reuse the story, doll design or wording.
title_pattern: 'New Household Rules (Pt3?)' + 6 broad hashtags (#scary #fyp #trending #horrorstories #viral #animatic). Pattern: [New/Updated] [Place] Rules + part number. 'Rules' promises a list of instructions that the viewer is pulled into; 'Household' puts it in the viewer's own home; 'Pt3?' (with a question mark) shows it is a series and invites the 'where are part 1/2?' binge and comment. Titles barely matter on Shorts, but a 'X Rules' title tells people what they're getting and is easy to turn into a series: 'Babysitting Rules', 'Night Shift Rules', 'Hotel Rules Pt 2'.

thumbnail.source: YouTube auto-picked frame from ~46.5 s (the B&W cracked-doll reveal with 'THANK THE DOLL'), shown 1280x720 as a 9:16 frame pillarboxed over a blurred, darkened copy of itself. In the Shorts feed the vertical frame is what viewers see.
thumbnail.composition: One centred subject filling the frame: a porcelain doll from the waist up with the face in the top third, two huge black hollow eye sockets, a crack running across the forehead and cheek, and a small dark smiling mouth. A bright white blown-out smear (her hand / a light flare) sits low centre-left. The caption sits at about 70% height, right over her chest.
thumbnail.text: 'THANK THE DOLL': a scratchy hand-drawn all-caps horror font, white with 'DOLL' in red and a thin dark outline.
thumbnail.colours: Fully desaturated grey scale (mid-grey background, near-black hair and dress, white face), with one red word as the only colour. The video's own palette is warm red/mint before the reveal, so the cover frame is deliberately the 'wrong', drained version.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: The face of a large, close doll fills about 45% of the frame against a plain flat background; the black eye sockets are the strongest contrast points (pure black on white). There is no other subject.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Uncanny-valley doll face with empty eyes is a cheap, reliable fear trigger that reads even as a thumbnail; the grey scale stands out in a colourful feed; the line 'Thank the doll' is an odd instruction that makes people curious. Note that frame 0 (the skull-apple with 'LISTEN CAREFULLY') is the first frame people see while scrolling, and the doll is the cover image in search and on the channel page, so the video has two strong images.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: Listen carefully and act fast. First, check around you.
hook.verbatim_5_to_14s: Make sure your red doll and the flashlight are nearby. If you can't find the doll, peek under the bed. Catch her before she runs away.
hook.device: An urgent order spoken straight to the viewer (second person, imperative, 'act fast') with no setup. It drops the viewer into a survival situation as the person following the rules. The first rule refers to 'your red doll' as if the viewer already owns it (presupposition: there's no explanation, you are already inside the story). At 11 s comes the first wrongness: 'Catch her before she runs away' means the doll moves on its own. Visual: frame 0 is a full-bleed, saturated horror icon (melting red apple-skull with one glowing green eye) with the hook text drawn twice (top and bottom), the only full-frame colour image until the reveal; it cuts to black at 2.7 s and then into the letterboxed illustrated story.

beats.summary: 'Listen carefully and act fast.' Urgent second-person order over a skull-apple horror image; it sets up the rules format and the time pressure.
Check around you; make sure your red doll and flashlight are nearby. This brings in the protective object (the doll) and a tool, treating the viewer as already inside the situation.
If the doll is missing, look under the bed and 'catch her before she runs away'. The protective object is alive, the first jolt of wrongness. The text card glitches out to black.
Check the doll for damage; 'It's okay if you find any.' The calm reassurance hints that damage is expected (the doll gets hurt protecting you), which sets up the payoff.
A box has appeared next to the white closet 'now'. Do not open it; 'You're not ready for what's inside yet.' This open loop is never closed and acts as a hook for the series.
Before opening the door, peek through the crack. 'Do you see anything strange?' A direct question to the viewer, with a glitch, then a flash of a pale face.

If you do, close your eyes, put the doll on the door for 10 seconds, then open your eyes. Near-black screen with a faint ghost face drifting in the dark, ending in the only silence (0.4 s) before the reveal.

'If the doll looks different, you're safe to open the door. The danger is gone.' Reveal: the cute doll from 14 s is now cracked, with empty eyes, in the same pose (a callback shot). The image breaks out of the letterbox to full frame, with a chroma glitch at 44 s.
'...at least for now.' A shaky, doubled text card on black takes back the relief.

'Thank the doll, even though she probably can't save you anymore.' B&W doll close-up with a smeared zoom-blur rush, then black with 'CAN'T SAVE YOU ANYMORE'. It ends on dread, not resolution, which suits the series and a replay.

pacing.words_per_caption_card: 2-4 (one short phrase at a time, never a full sentence)
pacing.illustration_holds_s: 3-5.5 s per illustrated still (7 distinct illustrations in 50 s), with black text-only cards of 0.5-2.5 s between them; about 30% of runtime is black screen with only a caption
pacing.rehook_interval_s: about 5-7 s: a new rule or instruction every sentence pair; wrongness beats at 11 (doll runs), 18 (damage is okay), 24 (do not open), 31 (anything strange?), 39 (doll changed), 45 (for now), 48 (can't save you)
pacing.notes: Calm, measured delivery (162 wpm, slower than story-narration horror at 200-230 wpm) with short pauses at sentence breaks. The order 'act fast' is in the words, not in the speed of the voice. The one silence (0.4 s) comes right before the reveal. Ending at 49.9 s on a black card helps it loop.

techniques_worth_copying: Second-person 'rules' format: every line is an instruction to YOU, so the viewer is the protagonist. No characters to introduce and no backstory; it can be scaled into a series (Household Rules Pt1..N, Night Shift Rules, Babysitter Rules).
Presupposition hook: 'Make sure YOUR red doll...' treats the viewer as already in the story. Skipping the explanation creates instant immersion and curiosity.

A protective object that becomes the victim: the friendly talisman (doll) takes the damage. The 14 s insert shot is repeated at 39 s in the same pose, but corrupted. A setup/payoff callback that needs only one new image.
Unsettling reassurance lines ('It's okay if you find any', 'The danger is gone, at least for now') are scarier than direct threats because they suggest what is left unsaid.
An unresolved open loop for the series ('there should be a box now... you're not ready for what's inside yet').
A direct question to the viewer at the scariest moment ('Do you see anything strange?'), followed by a flash frame of a face.

Breaking the format for the reveal: the story plays in a 16:9 letterbox inside 9:16, and the reveal and ending suddenly fill the whole frame and switch to B&W. A strong visual 'something changed' with no extra assets.
Black-screen text cards as rhythm and as a substitute for shots: about 30% of runtime is black with a caption. Cheap, builds dread, and forces reading.
Keyword colour coding in captions: white scratchy horror font with the important words in red (danger, the doll) and one object in green (box). Gives emphasis without changing size.

Caption micro-effects tied to meaning: RGB-split on 'runs away', dim low-opacity whisper text for 'not ready', jittery double-vision text for 'at least for now', a big red slam over the image for 'DO NOT OPEN IT'.
Two-image identity: a saturated horror icon as frame 0 (skull apple) for the scroll-stop, and a desaturated creepy doll as the cover frame for browsing and search.
End on a gut-punch line plus a black card with no CTA, so the video loops seamlessly into 'Listen carefully...' again.

code_only_remake_requirements.assets: About 7-8 still illustrations as SVG/vector scenes (or flat-shaded procedural): a hero 'icon' title image (any horror emblem, e.g. a cracked object with one glowing eye), a protagonist in 3-4 poses (peeking from a blanket, under a bed, standing by a wardrobe with a box, eye at a door crack), a protective-object insert in a clean and a corrupted version (same layout, swap the face layer: big glossy eyes -> black hollow sockets plus crack paths), and a dim ghost face. The corrupted version can be made from the clean one with SVG filters plus extra crack paths, so it is one asset with two states.
code_only_remake_requirements.layout: 1080x1920 black canvas; story images in a centred 1080x608 (16:9) band at y=540-1150; captions centred under the band at y about 1210-1300; reveal and ending shots switch to full-bleed 1080x1920.
code_only_remake_requirements.camera: Slow Ken Burns push-in (scale 1.00->1.06 over 4-5 s) on each still; very small 'animatic' tweens (a head turn of 2-4 px, a blink) are optional; a fast zoom-blur rush for the final scare (scale 1->1.6 over 1.5 s plus motion blur or a stretched clone stack).
code_only_remake_requirements.transitions: Hard cuts, cuts to black (0.3-0.6 s), one 0.6 s crossfade, a single flash frame (2-3 frames of pale noise texture with a faint face), and an RGB-split / block-displacement glitch (offset red and cyan copies of the layer, random horizontal slice offsets, scan lines) at 12 s, 31 s and 44 s.
code_only_remake_requirements.captions: Word-timed caption cards of 2-4 words from TTS timestamps; scratchy handwritten horror display font (e.g. a free 'scratchy marker' Google font such as 'Rubik Wet Paint', 'Creepster' or 'Nosifer'-lite; pick one licensed for use), white with a thin black stroke, with per-word colour tags (red for threat/talisman words, green for one object). Effect variants: chroma-split, low-opacity whisper, double-vision jitter, big slam over the image.
code_only_remake_requirements.colour_grading: Warm red/teal/mint palette for the 'safe' illustrations; CSS/SVG filters for the corruption state: saturate(0.3) then grayscale(1) plus contrast(1.4) for the ending; vignette overlay; film grain/noise texture.
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Calm second-person TTS voice (Kokoro/Piper) at about 160 wpm; a low ambient drone bed, a soft hit on the reveal, a glitch SFX on each RGB-split, one 0.4 s silence before the reveal. Mix mean about -21 dB, peaks near 0 dB.
code_only_remake_requirements.script_template: [Order hook 3 s] -> [rule 1: check talisman + presupposed setting] -> [rule 1b: talisman moves on its own] -> [rule 2: inspect damage + creepy reassurance] -> [rule 3: forbidden new object, 'not ready yet' open loop] -> [rule 4: threat at a threshold + direct question] -> [ritual with eyes closed + darkness] -> [reveal: talisman corrupted = safe] -> [undercut 'for now'] -> [gut-punch closer] in 45-60 s, about 130-150 words. Write original rules, objects and settings.
code_only_remake_requirements.effort_estimate: Low-medium: no lip-sync, no character animation, 7-8 static scenes; the main effort is illustration quality (vector art that reads as 'creepy-cute') and the glitch/caption effect components, which can be reused for every episode.
